task.description:
Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's amendment (new S2.5 section) to lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md, per WF-02 Step 1b's same procedure applied to this amendment. You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921 -- verify with git branch --show-current, pull if needed. Read the amended design section directly. Verify: (1) the empty-declared_fields behavior (skip both violation classes, return {valid: true, violations: []}) is stated explicitly with real reasoning, not asserted; (2) the amendment's own claim that all 10 original acceptance criteria remain unaffected is actually verified -- re-check AC1-AC6 yourself against the actual test scenarios TEST-DESIGNER wrote (test/specs/REQ-372.md and the two test files) to confirm none of them exercises the definition with an EMPTY declared_fields map in a way that would now silently pass when it should still fail; (3) no implementation code (function bodies) was introduced by the amendment -- signature/behavior description only; (4) the fix genuinely resolves the diagnosed root cause without requiring any pre-existing fixture to be modified -- read handoffs/WF02-REQ372-20260921/step-03-test-designer.json's failure evidence and confirm the amendment's mechanism (guard inside validate/2 itself, applying uniformly to both call sites) actually closes that gap by construction. FAIL immediately on any check failure.

RE-GATE (rework iteration 1 addressed): CODE-DESIGNER has revised S2.5.4 to (a) honestly acknowledge the three conflicting tests instead of falsely claiming compatibility, and (b) added S2.5.4.1 stating explicitly that TEST-DESIGNER must revise those three tests' expectations, with the specific corrected expectation named for each. Re-read the design fresh and confirm: does S2.5.4/S2.5.4.1 now genuinely and specifically resolve the conflict (naming each test, its current wrong-under-the-amendment assertion, and its required new assertion) rather than just gesturing at 'tests need updating'? Is the reasoning for the AC6 reverse-test's revised approach (a different before/after pair that never ends in an empty schema, rather than just weakening the assertion) sound? This is a re-gate of the same design/reasoning question, not a new implementation to review.
acceptance_criteria: empty-declared_fields behavior stated explicitly with reasoning
AC1-AC6 compatibility independently re-verified against the actual test scenarios, not just CODE-DESIGNER's own claim
no implementation code introduced by the amendment
the amendment's mechanism plausibly closes the 31-fixture regression without requiring fixture edits
the three test-conflict scenarios are now explicitly and specifically reconciled (named test, current assertion, required new assertion, reasoning) -- not just acknowledged in passing

result.summary:
Re-gate iteration 2, fresh read of the revised §2.5 (including new §2.5.4 correction and new §2.5.4.1) in lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md. All five re-gate acceptance criteria hold.

(1) empty-declared_fields behavior: unchanged from iteration 1, still stated explicitly with real reasoning in §2.5.1/§2.5.2 -- skip both violation classes, return {valid: true, violations: []} unconditionally when declared_fields == %{}.

(2) AC1-AC6 independently re-verified against the actual committed test files: §2.5.4 has been corrected -- it no longer asserts (falsely) that AC1-AC6's test cases never reach the empty-declared_fields branch. It now explicitly names the same three conflicts this validator found in iteration 1, cites their exact file paths and line numbers, and cross-references §2.5.4.1 for the resolution. Independently re-checked the three cited tests against the current committed source (test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs:106 and test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:211,241 -- exact line numbers confirmed via grep, matching the design doc precisely) and confirm the design's description of each test's current assertions is accurate.

(3) No implementation code introduced: confirmed by re-scan of the full §2.5 block (lines 357-632) -- the only fenced code block is the unchanged @spec signature line for validate/2 (a type signature, not a body). §2.5.4.1's guidance to TEST-DESIGNER is prose describing required assertion changes, not implementation code.

(4) Mechanism still plausibly closes the 31-fixture regression without fixture edits: §2.5.3's guard placement (inside validate/2, uniform across both call sites) is unchanged from iteration 1; §2.5.4.1 explicitly confirms none of the three test revisions touch semantic_validation.ex, definitions.ex, or any of the ~31 pre-existing fixtures.

(5) Three test-conflict scenarios now explicitly and specifically reconciled: §2.5.4.1 is genuinely specific, not a vague gesture. For each of the three named tests it states (a) the exact current assertion (e.g. test 1: `[message] = messages(result)` expecting exactly one violation; test 2: `{:ok, %{valid: false, violations: violations}}` plus an `Enum.any?(..., :undeclared_variable_reference)` check; test 3: `valid: false` with the same violation code via validate_definition_graph/2), (b) the required new assertion (test 1: `messages(result) == []`; tests 2 and 3: offers a preferred fix -- reseed with a non-empty declared_fields that still omits the referenced field, e.g. seed 'customer_name' instead of 'amount', preserving a genuine §2.2 violation -- and a weaker acceptable fallback of asserting {valid: true, violations: []} directly), and (c) reasoning tied back to §2.5.1's policy (an empty schema is a legitimate current state, not itself evidence of an undeclared-reference intent). Independently re-verified test 3's preferred fix is mechanically sound: grep of semantic_validation_activation_test.exs confirms the gateway condition is 'amount > 100' (graph_referencing_amount/0, line 99-113), so seeding 'customer_name' instead of 'amount' does leave declared_fields non-empty while 'amount' remains genuinely undeclared against it -- an ordinary §2.2 violation, not the §2.5.1 exemption, exactly as claimed.

AC6 reverse-test reasoning re-verified as sound: the design's preferred fix (§2.5.4.1 item 2, first bullet) uses a different before/after pair that never enters the empty-declared_fields branch at all (seed 'customer_name' only, so the gateway's 'amount' reference is a genuine non-empty-schema violation for the first call; then seed 'amount' and assert success for the second) rather than weakening the assertion on an empty-schema call, which is exactly what the RE-GATE task instruction asked to confirm. This preserves AC6's actual guarantee (fresh call reflects current state, not cached) throughout, and the weaker fallback option is clearly marked as the less-preferred alternative with its own honest tradeoff stated (no longer illustrates a violation-to-clean transition).

No new implementation-code, scope-creep, or reasoning-soundness issues found in this iteration.
